title: HELIOS agent-fleet topology v2 (config/fleet/fleet-topology.json)
description: Declarative pool layout (docs/architecture/HERMES_FLEET_AND_XCORE.md). Bound read-only by src/ai/HELIOS.AIHub/Fleet/FleetTopology.cs (version, pools[].name / taskTypes / providerChain / hermesFleet); scripts/fleet/start-fleet.ps1 reads defaults.spawn and each pool's hermesFleet / assigneePrefix / taskTypes, scripts/fleet/scale-fleet.ps1 merges each pool's autoscaling over defaults.autoscaling. version is pinned to 2: a v3 layout gets a v3 schema, not a silently half-read file. Objects are closed so a misspelled key (maxLocalLane, providerchain) fails here instead of falling back to a default at run time; every object accepts a $comment.

pools.description: Every per-pool ceiling in this schema is per pool, and `helios-fleet start` selects them all: without a bound on the array, 1,000 pools of 64 workers validated and asked one host for 64,000 processes. Four times the shipped layout. The aggregate worker and burst-lane totals are bounded as well, by the semantic rule the schema cannot express (validate_config_schemas.py, ManifestSemantics).

taskType.description: A config/aihub.json taskRouting key: a bare task type, or one qualified by a normalized language (`<taskType>:<language>`, one ':' at most) exactly as TaskTypeRoutingStrategy.RoutingKey spells it; FleetPlanService splits a qualified pool task type before its learning read.

poolSize.description: Cap applied by scripts/fleet/start-fleet.ps1 in workspace mode (Codespaces / Cloud Shell); per pool, else inherited from defaults, else half the declared size rounded up. 64 is the same ceiling start-fleet.ps1 enforces on -PoolSize: a topology value bypasses that parameter check and spawns this many worker processes.

lanes.description: A lane THRESHOLD, not a capacity: scale-fleet.ps1 compares it and casts it to [int], so the bound is the cast's. Capacity fields use laneCapacity / burstCapacity instead.

laneCapacity.description: Worker processes scale-fleet.ps1 may start on the operator's own host for one pool: the reconciler derives its delta straight from these and spawns a process per lane, so the ceiling is the same 64 start-fleet.ps1 enforces on -PoolSize. A topology is config, and config should not be able to fork two billion workers.

burstCapacity.description: Lanes a pool may add on ARC burst capacity, which scale-fleet.ps1 aggregates into `az vmss scale --new-capacity`: paid cloud capacity, so it is bounded well above any shipped pool (8) and far below a number that would bill by accident.

argsTemplate.description: Must carry the {prompt} slot; {assignee} is substituted when present. Passed as argv, never through a shell.

mode.description: hybrid = warm local lanes plus ARC burst; local = never burst; cloud = never run locally.

scaleDownIdleSeconds.description: Idle seconds before scaling down; read as an [int] by scale-fleet.ps1.

hermesFleet.description: Per pool, else inherited from defaults.hermesFleet (scripts/fleet/scale-fleet.ps1, learn-fleet.ps1); board defaults to the pool name and maxConcurrentLanes to the scripts' own cap, so neither is required here.

maxConcurrentLanes.description: Concurrent Hermes lanes for the pool. Bound to a C# int (HermesFleetOptions.MaxConcurrentLanes): a larger value fails FleetTopology.TryLoad outright, and the fleet scripts cast it to [int] before applying the cap.

poolSize.description: Worker processes per pool unless a pool overrides it; 64 is the ceiling start-fleet.ps1 enforces on -PoolSize, applied here too because a topology value bypasses that check.
Worker processes for this pool; the same 64 ceiling as -PoolSize in start-fleet.ps1.

providerChain.description: Ordered provider / CLI-agent names from config/aihub.json; first is primary.
